en:
She said "Only the stone survives." 

Show her the Mountain Soul?
The condition of the nearby bones suggests that this person was taken down violently from behind, perhaps by one of the creatures you've fought.
There is a dreadful miasma rising up out of the stairwell. Whatever has corrupted the temple lies below.
This chest appears to have been broken into already. It looks as though whoever it was hastily stashed some things inside.
This wall appears to be very weak. If you had a pickaxe, you could probably break through it.
This wall is in very poor condition. You might be able to get through it with your pickaxe.
You show the Dryad the Mountain Soul.
Something doesn't seem right.
This ominous chest is securely locked. Perhaps the key is somewhere in the rubble.
This pile of rubble is still smouldering. Search through it?
A strange vibration ripples through the air as you touch the gate.
Now that you have a moment to examine the gate latch, you can see that it's only tied shut with a heavy rope. It takes you a moment, but you are able to undo the knot, and the gate falls open.
The enchantment is stronger than you expected. You'll need to try again more carefully.
There are still several useful items on his body. He certainly won't be needing them.
This body is crumpled and withered, seemingly by unnatural means. Who knows what these witches have done to him?
This crystal appears to be an anchor for an enchantment. Someone of sufficient skill could unravel it.

"Well, you've been a big help. Taking that lift shaves days off my travel time, and based on some of the stuff we saw out the window, probably weeks of recovery time too. Thanks again, and try not to get killed."
Skyway closed for maintenance
Chuckling to himself, Paul casually puts his axe down, kicks his boots off, undoes his belts, and drops his clothes to the floor, stepping out of them with proud ease.
Eventually, you roll out your bedrolls on the raised frames and settle in for a restful night.
Everyone seems to have slept well. Paul and Peregrine seem to be in particularly high spirits.
Peregrine looks on slackjawed as Paul poses for him shamelessly.
Peregrine seems especially happy to share the moment with everyone.
The better part of the evening is spent sitting with your friends in the small bath chamber, chatting and washing the marks of the long road off of each others' skin.
The shelter is a little musty, but it is dry and well-protected. You lay your bedrolls out on the wooden frames, and the night passes without further incident.
As you pull together the threads of mana, something seems to be out of place. You realize at the last moment that the spell is a trap, and you are blasted with a wave of violent energy.
Some runes have been etched into the wall. It appears to be an incomplete spell, commonly used in magically-sealed passageways. A competent weaver should be able to open the passage.
The decoy runes vanish, leaving no trace of your folly but for the throbbing in your arm.
The drapery on this sculpture is masterfully crafted. Clearly the work of a skilled artisan.
The handiwork on this sculpture is so fine that there are no tooling marks showing.
The magical runes crackle and dissipate. Whatever may have been concealed here is forever beyond your reach.
The proportions of the woman depicted in this sculpture are sublime.
This statue is intricately carved, the marble clothing looks almost translucent over the female form.
You fumble through the spell and the magic fizzles. You should probably be able to attempt it again, however.

You weave the threads of mana together into perfect formation, and the spell is complete. The wall vanishes into thin air, revealing a vault carved in alabaster marble. It appears to have lain undisturbed for ages.
Inside this chest is a magnificent whip, throbbing with uneasy energy.
As you approach, the lips on the statue begin to move, and it whispers to you in a grainy voice.
Feed 12000$ to the statue?
It takes nearly two hours to feed all of the money in through the mouth of the statue, but as you do, bit by bit, golden stairs appear before you, bridging the chasm cleanly.
The statue appears to be broken.
The statue's mouth yawns open.
The smell is reminiscent of the fluid you found when you started exploring Chrun.
A light shock shivers through your body. Touching the fluid must have somehow connected you with the nerves of this place for a split second, almost as if the walls were part of your own body.
A thick rope of nervous tissue is stretched between the floor and the ceiling.
He surely won't be needing his supplies any longer.
Seems whoever this was got walled in and couldn't escape.
There is a churning pool of thick, foul fluid here. It seems fresher here than at the nerve bundles.
You dunk a bottle into the fluid and collect some of it.
You felt the ground and walls shudder, but there is no obvious change.
An impressive statue of a man. While it is only roughly carved, all the features of the body are clearly defined.

On the other side of the wall you can hear some movement. The wall here is still quite solid, but appears cracked enough that a strong physical or magical blow could break through. Attempt using your strength or magical prowess?
The contents of the chest have all been taken, likely by that annoying goblin.
There is nothing left to be found within this chest.
Upon further inspection, you find a button on the pillar of the statue underneath the arm of the man. When you press it, you hear a loud rumbling noise as the wall nearby opens up.
You find... nothing.
You manage to force through the wall, and when the dust settles, you find that it leads to the tomb where the goblin disappeared.
You manage to force through the wall, to reveal a hidden tomb. In addition, you end up surprising the goblin who was still trying to place the contents of the chests into his sack.
You peer into the chest, and possibly due to the surprise of you breaking down the tomb wall, the goblin had missed an emerald.
A few spare coins remain in this cabinet.
There are several ancient, rusted tools in this cabinet, probably used for woodworking.
This heavily-eroded statue depicts the body of an idealized man. Its details have been smoothed away over time, but a name can still be read along the base.
This signpost is faded too badly to be legible, but it seems to be indicating that this building is a shop.
A bit of glinting metal catches your eye amid the mushrooms in this patch.

A mouth-watering aroma sends your head into a spin when you approach this patch of mushrooms. Sitting amid less remarkable varieties is a white truffle, widely renowned for its delicate texture and intoxicating flavor.
Amid the mushrooms in this patch, you find a variety that is edible, if not delicious.
Approaching this mushroom patch apparently upsets the creatures milling about. They all turn toward you and attack.
Approaching this mushroom patch apparently upsets the large mushroom creature nearby. It and its kin all turn toward you and attack.
As you approach the sack, something rushes at you from behind!
As you poke around this mushroom patch, something quivers and lurches up out of the ground toward you!
From atop this pillar, you could probably climb to the ledge above, however, it does not look sturdy, and it would not be an easy climb.
He pauses a moment, sniffing the air conspicuously. It seems you're carrying something that he is especially interested in - probably the rare white truffle you have in your pockets.
No sooner does the last person arrive however, than you spot a groggy giant scrambling for his weapon. It seems you've interrupted someone's nap.
Picking up the sack, you discover another climbing chain hidden under it. In the sack itself is a handful of coins, but nothing else of note.
Seeing your reflection in the crystal clear water, you can see that the last few battles have left you rather filthy. The fountain is practically inviting you to wash your face.
The giant's lone eye narrows as you back away. He charges, apparently deciding to take what he wants off of your corpse.
The pillar is more fragile than you expected, and crumbles out from beneath your feet before you have a chance to reach the upper ledge.
The pillar is practically disintegrating beneath your feet, but you manage to use what's left of it to climb up, and you take a moment to help your party follow.
There is a broken column of stone here, and it is irregular enough to make for easy climbing to the ledge above.
There is a chain anchored to the cliff here. You could use it to easily drop to the ledge below.
This rock is firmly anchored. If you had a rope, you could climb to the lower ledge from here.
This rock is firmly anchored. If you lower your rope, you could easily climb down to the ledge below.
When you reach the lower ledge, you see a number of mushrooms with faces waddling around. They have seen you, but do not seem to be particularly concerned.
You hold out the white truffle to the giant, who snatches it out of your hand and noisily scarfs it down. A look of mellow euphoria washes over him - he isn't a threat at the moment.
You light the signal fire to indicate to the rest of your band that this area has been secured.
You poke around the mushroom patch, but don't find anything edible.
You've caught him in a foul mood, it seems. He charges straight at you.
It reads : This is a holy sanctuary. Entry is prohibited to all but our brothers.
The chunk of slag you are carrying comes to mind. Will you place the Paladin Soul upon the pedestal?
This pedestal is caked with flaking rust. There is an inscription on the very top.
You decide to hold on to the Paladin Soul for now. Perhaps it can be of use elsewhere.
You make an offering of the Paladin Soul, a bit of slag forged from the destruction of many weapons.

"Do you have any idea what the word "Portas" means? A madman came through here a while ago, and it was carved into his skin in several places. He was too crazed to answer me when I asked, but I can't stop thinking about it."
"Here's your meal. I really should not have done that though, so if you want more, it's straight coin, sorry!"
"How are you supposed to have any privacy when fools keep walking in and interrupting?"
"Sorry, but I am not available right now. Go bother someone else."
"What part of "Hands to your Damn Self" do you have trouble understanding?"
As you get close to the mushrooms, the man nearby speaks up.
Peering into the crate, you see rows of potion bottles. Extending a hand towards the crate, the man nearby growls a low warning.
The guard dismissively waves you away, buried in his paperwork.
The guard is grumbling over his gigantic stack of paperwork.
There isn't anything that jumps out at you.
These plants look ready to pick, and could prove useful.
This chest is empty.
You are pricked by the plant's sharp thorns.
You dozed off for a few moments, and wake up alone. Your meal is wrapped up neatly on the floor nearby with an attached note.
You leaf through several of the books piled on this shelf. After a moment, the barkeep approaches you.
You share a carefree romp on a mountain of pillows in a dark corner upstairs. It's obvious that he doesn't get this opportunity very often, and he is very enthusiastic.
You hear a strange noise.
"... yeah I know."
"Excellent! This will be a perfect distraction from the wet chill."
A scrap of paper with a note is sitting inside the open drawer here.
After drying off by the fire, you all avail yourselves of the huts and the night passes without further incident.
After the fire dies down, you all avail yourselves of the huts, and the night passes without further incident.
Bato beams at the compliment and quietly busies himself with preparing the food, while Greave shoots you a conspiratory glance, a sheepish grin showing through his beard.
Bato clears his throat.
Bato fixes a smug gaze on Greave while he starts chopping up the vegetables.
Bato is puffing himself out proudly in characteristic fashion.
Both Bato and Greave are looking at you expectantly.
Greave closes his eyes and hurriedly strips off his pants, throwing them on the ground near the fire with a wet slap. His face is bright red.
Greave looks at you, exasperated.
Greave seems uncomfortable for a while, but as the night wears on and the warmth of the fire soaks into his skin, his posture relaxes and his familiar smile returns to his face.
In the morning, everyone is dry and dressed, and when everyone is ready to go, Greave playfully reaches out and scratches Bato's chest.
It seems like today is off to a good start.
The conversation is lively, and you enjoy an easy night chatting by the fire with two of the finest friends you've made in recent memory.
The food isn't wonderful, but Bato does the best he can with what is at hand.
There is a note tied to this sack.
When the fire dies and it comes time to retire, Greave stands, defiantly displaying his body to both of you one last time before laughing and forfeiting the contest to his opponent.

You devise all kinds of comparisons to put the two men through, measuring the width, thickness, and loft of the hair covering both their bodies, but eventually the contest breaks down into laughing and swapping stories.
It reads : Only those who dare appraise a life against coin may enter.
The chunk of slag you are carrying comes to mind. Will you place the Mercenary Soul upon the pedestal?
The pedestal is worn with moisture and caked with dried on salt. There is an inscription on the very top.
You decide to hold on to the Mercenary Soul for now. Perhaps it can be of use elsewhere.
You make an offering of the Mercenary Soul, a bit of slag forged from the destruction of many weapons.
After a long moment, however, nothing happens.
An old armour mannequin. This one is underneath the eave of the shop, so it is in much better condition than its weather-exposed neighbor.
Faxford's Alchemical Wonders

Hammond and Sons
Steelcrafters

Special Orders Available
Free Beer with Armour Repair
It's a blacksmith's workshop.
It's an old armour mannequin. It was probably well-used even before weather and neglect ravaged it.

Mercarie's Fine Vestments

Fashion for any Occasion!
Serena Diddler's Chiropracty and Physician
Stephan's Crystal and Gemcraft
Tem Shop
There is a suspicious amount of seating in the street with direct line of sight to the blacksmith's workstation. Hmm.
There's nothing inside but a few scraps of cloth.
This old tailor's shop is full of various mannequins. Some of them are so realistic that you half expect them to move.
You feel uncomfortable, as though you are being watched.
You have no idea what a "Tem" is.
A shiver runs down your spine.

After a moment, the book begins to swell and blister, and upon the completion of Borgnina's prayer, it bursts into a column of ash. 

Nothing is left except for a jagged mass of black stone.

After only a moment, he's eaten the entire thing. 

Zantanak pulls a glistening, black chunk of stone out of his mouth and hands it to you.
Borgnina reaches into her hood and plucks out a lock of her hair. Laying it in a wreath around the bizarre book, she takes a moment to whisper a prayer.
The moment you flip open the book, the pages fly apart and the book is gone.
There is a strange book sitting on the table here. It is bound in a thin, pale leather, and carries a sharp odour.
Zantanak takes the book from the table, and without opening it, he lifts it to his face and begins to eat it.
There is a plaque which is still legible.
It reads : Only a heartless killer would dare step forward.
The chunk of slag you are carrying comes to mind. Will you place the Assassin Soul upon the pedestal?
The pedestal is engraved with an unrecognizable script. There is one part you can read on the very top.
You decide to hold on to the Assassin Soul for now. Perhaps it can be of use elsewhere.
You make an offering of the Assassin Soul, a bit of slag forged from the destruction of many weapons.
In the lantern light, you can see that one side of the bed is heavily bowed, as though the person who slept on this side was much, much heavier.
Moria just sighs and shakes her head.
The father has a large, goofy grin with exaggerated teeth.
The whimsical decorations on this chest seem to mark it as a child's toybox. There are still a few mouldering toys inside, and they appear to be all very boyish.

There is a stack of paper and charcoal in this end table. There are what appear to be children's drawings on some of the pages. There are five figures holding hands, apparently the very picture of a happy family.
There is still a bit of fuel in this lantern.
This fuel in this furnace is mouldering and damp.
At the very least it is an expensive luxury item. Perhaps someone will buy it.
It appears as though this area was used for some kind of public event.
The axe lodged in this stump appears to be very thoroughly stuck, but you might be able to free it if you are strong enough.
The old wood complains loudly as you wedge the axe free, but come free it does. Its home in the stump has seemingly protected its edge from the rust that covers its heel.
The table is covered with dirty bottles, most of them empty, but one still has its stopper on tight. It doesn't appear to be a potion, but rather an aromatic extracted from flowers.
The wooden panel gives way with a crunch, revealing the room sealed behind.
There is a rusted key inside the drawer here.
This cauldron is full of scummy, stagnant rainwater, and is seething with bug larvae. It hasn't been used in a very long time.
This panel was meant to block off a passage behind it, but it is not subtle. A good heave might see it come loose.
Try as you might, the axe will not budge. Perhaps someone stronger should make the attempt.
You are unable to get an adequate grip on the panel.
He closes his eyes and takes a sharp breath. For a few long moments, he just breathes, until eventually he reaches up with a grubby hand and fondles the amulet gently.
His hand is trembling.
The goblin from before is gone.
The goblin looks up at you with desperate eyes, too weak to move.
There is a goblin here, slumped against the wall in the firelight. He is clearly distraught, weak, and not a threat to you.
There is a plain-looking amulet on the altar here, arranged purposefully. It seems as though it was to be used for some sort of ritual.
This urn contains several bottles, most of them broken, but one appears to still be sealed tightly.
When he notices you, he croaks out a whispered plea, and points to his neck. You can see there is a clean band of skin about his throat, as though he had been wearing something that was removed.
With the last of the undead silenced, you are able to take the amulet from the altar.
You fasten the amulet around the goblin's neck, and it settles into the clean spot.
That book is the only clue you have. You'd better take it with you.
The floor is laid out in a ceremonial medallion. Words are carved into the outer ring.
The temple behind you is beginning to fill with water. There's no going back now.
There is a chute in the chasm above you here. You are able to climb up through it by using these high rocks as a stepping stone.
There is a loud rumble from the other room. The book falls off the table and onto the floor.

This statue has an inscription around the base. It reads : 
"I will watch as you suffer and die."

This statue has an inscription around the base. It reads : 
"The color of blood is pleasing to my eyes."
You cough half the sea out of your lungs and onto the floor of the grotto. Though every part of you burns with pain, you are alive and breathing.
You find yourself in a sprawling, labyrinthine tunnel with no indication of which way might lead to an exit.
You have no idea where you are, however, and it appears that you are alone and without a torch.
You spot a small book resting on the corner of the table.
Your body is dashed hard against stone, and you are suddenly jarred to your senses.
"After a long while, the sense of his presence begins to diminish, and you get the feeling he has gone back to sleep."
A pair of unseen hands surveys your body impatiently.
Stumbling through the darkness, the path seems to make no sense. It is difficult to tell if you are making progress at all.
The unseen owner of the voice is skilled and accomodating, and while he is careful not to harm you, he eagerly collects his due."
There is a slight sparkle from the edge of this dusty old shelf.
You disrobe and crawl into the bed. The sheets are cold and the room is black as pitch.
You find a single gilded key, dangling from a hook.
You put your clothes back on and rejoin the others. It seems you have earned your safety.
Demons of all stripes continue to mingle and revel around you.

Every demon in this place looks monstrous, but the throne is occupied by an ordinary-looking man. He is stark naked, his body splashed with thick tracts of black hair, and his beard is twisted into an improbable point.
For a long moment, you ponder the demon's offer, until he speaks up.
He catches your gaze, and his eyes shred through you from head to toe. There can be no doubt that this man, unassuming though he may appear, is a frightfully potent demon.
He makes a respectful gesture and calls out to you.
It is time to go.
Long minutes pass, or are they hours? You are perfectly warm and comfortable, your entire body glittering with a sensation somewhere between gruelling effort and orgasmic satisfaction.
One, however, you can read.
Suddenly you are reminded of your companions waiting for you back in the laboratory.

There are hands on your body, breath against your neck, teeth against your skin. Gravity rolls in a lazy tumble as your senses drink in throbbing firelight, warm, wet bodies, and the intoxicating mist of the pipe.
There are several books on the table written in languages you do not understand.
There is a communal hookah here. Will you take a puff?
You slump down onto a pile of cushions and relax. You are more comfortable than you have been in a long, long time.
You take a long drag from the pipe, and your head slips into a comfortable spin.
Your clothes have escaped you, your knees are weak, and there is a strange taste in your mouth. How long has it been?
An afternoon tea set is layed out on the table. At the center is a tiered tray lined with sweet treats.
The treehouse's construction seems fairly stable, but this section has been damaged quite badly. Twigs and leaves are scattered around the edges.
They all look quite tempting...
This seems like a comfortable place to take a nap. Would you like to rest a while?
